conflicts.description: PDF 13/14 name 6 playfield Shoot Again and 40 Ball in Play; PDF 51 marks 40 NOT USED, while PDF 41 draws backbox 9B6 BALL IN PLAY on column 1/row 6 (public 6). These are different pages of one manual, not independent corroboration. Photos 50030/50054 do not identify socket wiring, and the meaningful runtime 40 bit establishes no fitment. Resolution path: an owner or technician must trace an original model 521 insert-board Ball in Play socket to 9P1 and matrix columns/rows, including whether 6 has a shared backbox load; this requires physical access unavailable in the retained above-playfield/backglass photographs.

mechanisms.behavior: Two balls rest in the ball-ramp storage path on switches 10/11. Drain detection 9 prompts outhole 1 to return the ball; thrower 2 serves toward shooter trough 12, then a manual plunger launches it. The harness starts with 10/11 occupied and observes 2 on Start, and repeated 1 while 9 is held. Host ball moves are separate from coil causality. Exact storage geometry and retry timings remain unmeasured.
mechanisms.label: Two-ball storage, outhole and shooter

mechanisms.behavior: Saucer 23 retains the first ball for multiball while thrower 2 supplies the other. Release target 24 commands eject coil 3 and begins two-ball play. During multiball saucer entries score and eject immediately. The retained gameplay trace observes 2 with 23 held and 3 for 24 before host release of 23. A coil does not directly actuate its ball-presence switch; a ball moving after the kick changes it.
mechanisms.label: Eject-hole lock and release

mechanisms.behavior: Passive orbit entry spinner/rollunder and exit gate. Spinner-lane entry followed by exit gate completes orbit and triggers flash output 4. mechanisms.behavior: Rollunder contacts mark ramp entrance and exit. Completed ramp scores its lit value, mystery or extra ball. There is no moving ramp coil in Table 4. Do not confuse this shot ramp with the ball-storage ramp served by output 2.

mechanisms.behavior: FIREPOWER uses standup targets, not resettable drop targets. Letter groups and A-B-C-D lane completion control awards. The manual enumerates these contacts; the secondary feature count uses different categories and does not remove documented assemblies.
mechanisms.label: FIREPOWER standup targets and A-B-C-D lanes

Six special mappings, flipper synthesis, serve, orbit flash, saucer lock/release, drain and tilt are observed in gameplay. No trace establishes socket quantity, physical location, measured mechanical timing or Wild Texas compatibility. First switch run used 450ms holds and missed multiplexed numerals; sw-slow is its separate 2200ms successor.
